A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Customized-GRPO study. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original DreamBench experiments, component ablations, human evaluations, reward-model comparisons, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds an RPO comparison, further sensitivity analyses, and computational timing measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed method retains the same UNO/FLUX LoRA training, piecewise tanh-based Synergy-Aware Reward Shaping, Timestep-Aware Dynamic Weighting, and Algorithm 1. The additional experiments do not revise Customized-GRPO's procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 10,000-sample Syncd training subset and DreamBench evaluation coverage. The added RPO, sensitivity, and timing experiments reuse these data and the existing subject-driven generation task.

E2.justification: V2 adds UNO trained with RPO, attributed to Miao et al. (2024), to the DreamBench comparisons in Tables 1 and 2. Appendix A.2 describes its adaptation using the existing training data. The previously evaluated comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled weight-bound sweeps, crosses five synergy coefficients with standard and inverted TDW schedules, and specifies the added RPO preference-pair training protocol. The new efficiency comparison uses two SFT epochs versus one GRPO epoch. Existing DreamBench metrics, sampling, and human-evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing sensitivity studies with weight-bound testing and an explicit coefficient-by-schedule interaction analysis (Tables 4 and 5). Appendix C.2 adds training and inference efficiency analysis. These are focused additions to the already extensive component, reward-choice, conflict, and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain four generated images per evaluation prompt and the same human-rating aggregation procedures. V2 adds no seed reporting, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and human-evaluation results are retained. Added RPO scores are 0.852 DINO, 0.898 CLIP-I, 0.237 CLIP-T, and 4.47 HPS-v3. V2 also adds weight-bound, inverted-schedule, and timing entries. Table 5 partly redisplays Figure 6's existing results; it is not entirely new evidence.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13, the mathematical formulations of SARS and TDW, and the ODE-to-SDE discussion are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claim: SARS and TDW mitigate competitive degradation and improve the fidelity–editability balance. The new comparisons and analyses support this existing claim without redefining its scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of RPO's identity overfitting, failures under extreme weight bounds, and SARS's dependence on an appropriate TDW schedule. It also interprets training overhead and unchanged inference latency. The stated architecture and single-subject limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a repository pointer, specifies eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs and approximately 80 training hours/640 GPU-hours, and documents RPO preference-pair construction and efficiency-test budgets. Appendix A.1 also removes the 'per-GPU' qualification from batch size, reducing clarity without establishing an actual setting change.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to RPO, DPO, and PRISM, and explicitly positions its online approach against offline RPO. The related-work sections otherwise remain stable. The T2I-FactualBench reference changes from a preprint to its publication entry, representing the same cited work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized corrections, including GPRO to GRPO, expands Section 6.4, adds acknowledgments and an efficiency subsection, and moves qualitative results from C.2 to C.3. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4, 5, and 8, inserts RPO rows into Tables 1 and 2, and locally relocates existing displays. V1 Tables 4–5 become V2 Tables 6–7. All eleven figure images are unchanged; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added RPO comparison, targeted sensitivity tests, and implementation/timing disclosures make v2 more informative and reproducible. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Section 6.4 states inverted-TDW HPS-v3 is 0.3 while Table 5 reports 5.41–5.65, and Section 6.2 retains the highest-identity-score claim despite RPO's higher scores. The core method and existing evidence remain intact.
